conviction_note: The independent evidence on Q3 offsets: European peers that spoke after MAN's 16 Jul guide (Randstad, Adecco, Kelly) said growth momentum carried into Q3, the ASA/Bullhorn US indices were up y/y and EUR/USD ran slightly above its mid-July level. Against that, BLS temp help was revised to a Jul-Sep decline, Hays' Jul-Sep update showed Germany and the UK down, French PMI employment fell for a fifth month, and the revenue consensus sits at the top of the reported guide. Findings sum to +0.3 and the scaled number is +0.16 (p_up 51 on an 8% absolute move); the print will turn on the first Q4 EPS guide, which I could not source a bar for.
bar: Q3 2026 adj EPS $1.01 consensus (Earnings Whispers, whisper $1.03, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/MAN), which equals the company's guide midpoint ($0.96-1.06, 44% tax, -2c FX; 8-K ex99.1 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000871763/000119312526305399/man-ex99_1.htm). Other providers range from $0.96 (Zacks) to $1.05 (MarketBeat). Revenue consensus is $4.91bn (Earnings Whispers), at the top of the implied guide: +2-6% reported on Q3 2025's $4.63bn gives $4.72-4.91bn. The company also guided ~6% organic constant-currency growth at the midpoint, gross margin ~16% and EBITA margin up ~10bp y/y. No sourced Q4 2026 EPS consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,426,985 sh at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 9.5% of 46.51m shares outstanding, 5.38 days to cover. It was 13.45% (6.26m) at 2026-07-15 before the +32% July print, and has fallen steadily since: 10.24% at 08-31, 9.74% at 09-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/man/short-interest, read 2026-10-14). That is moderate and still meaningful for a squeeze on a beat. No skew: the option chain is unusable (ATM spread 162% of mid). Put/call OI ratio 0.98. The stock is -11.1% over 20 days and -2.6% over 5, -18% from its 52-week high and +100% from its low, so part of the reset into the print is already in the price.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after MAN's 16 Jul guide said Q3 started in growth. Randstad (22 Jul): Q2 organic +1.9% against 1% consensus, 'growth momentum continued into early Q3, most markets in growth', Southern Europe strong, Germany and UK back to growth. Adecco (6 Aug): Q2 organic +5.6%, Americas +12%, EMEA ex-France +8%, positive volume momentum into Q3. Kelly (6 Aug): beat its Q2 guide and raised its FY26 revenue outlook. Against that, Robert Half (23 Jul) guided Q3 flat y/y, with contract revenue -1% in early July. MAN's own guide calls for ~6% organic constant-currency growth at the midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue beat ($4.86bn vs ~$4.72bn) plus a Q3 guide: +32.4% on 2026-07-16. Q1 2026 in line: +0.9%. Q3 2025 beat with a soft Q4 guide: -6.5%. Revenue beats have paid when the guide confirmed them.
findings.why_not_priced: These are July-August statements, and consensus EPS ($1.01) sits exactly at the guide midpoint, so sell-side numbers have not visibly moved above the guide on them. If the market had priced Q3 momentum, consensus would sit above the midpoint and the stock would not be -11% over 20 days.
findings.independence: Adecco Q2 release https://www.adeccogroup.com/our-group/media/press-releases/q2-2026-results (2026-08-06); Kelly Q2 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000055135/000005513526000160/a20262qearningsreleaseform.htm (2026-08-06); Robert Half Q2 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000315213/000031521326000040/rhiq22026ex991.htm (2026-07-23, the offsetting voice). Four separate companies' documents.

findings.finding: US BLS temporary-help employment weakened through Q3 2026 after revisions: September -10,900 (the largest drop of the year), August revised to +200 from +6,800, and July flipped to -10,000. That is a net Jul-Sep decline of about 21k jobs. MAN guided US growth 'similar to Q2' (US +6% CC, Manpower US +16% days-adjusted).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history of MAN reacting to its US line alone. The US is roughly 15% of revenue, while France, Italy and the rest of Southern Europe are about half.
findings.why_not_priced: The revision landed on 2 Oct and the stock has fallen since ($56.28 on 2 Oct per trade-ideas, $51.49 now), so it is probably partly priced already. It is filed small, as a macro proxy for one segment of about 15% of revenue. What would have to go right in the rest: Southern Europe at ~4% CC and Latin America at ~24%, as in Q2.
findings.independence: Proxy only (snippet_only, page 403). Contradicted in part by the ASA and Bullhorn indices (next finding). MAN's own US business outgrew BLS temp help through H1.

findings.finding: Weekly US staffing indices stayed positive y/y through Q3. The ASA Staffing Index showed temp and contract employment +4.4% y/y for the four weeks to 16 Aug and +3.3% y/y in the week of 7-13 Sep. The SIA/Bullhorn indicator had hours +9% y/y in the week ending 26 Sep.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As above: the US line is about 15% of revenue and has no isolated reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: Weekly trade-association data that sell-side previews rarely cite. It is sized below the broader BLS series, which points the other way.
findings.independence: SIA/Bullhorn Staffing Indicator https://www.staffingindustry.com/research/research-reports/americas/sia-bullhorn-staffing-indicator-october-6-2026 (2026-10-06, snippet_only). This is a different survey from ASA.

findings.finding: Hays' first-quarter statement for July-September 2026 (12 Oct) showed group net fees -3% like-for-like. Temp and contracting fell 1% and perm 7%; Germany was -6% (temp volumes -2%), UK and Ireland -5%, US +8%. That is a direct same-quarter counterparty read on MAN's Northern Europe (UK, Germany, Nordics), which MAN guided 'largely stable to improving'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Northern Europe is about 17% of revenue and only just reached profitability in Q2 2026. There is no isolated reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out two days before the print and is a UK perm-heavy recruiter, so it is a weak read-through. Figures are from the SIA/asktraders write-ups of the RNS (https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/hays-q1-net-fee-decline-narrows-to-3-but-permanent-hiring-falls). MAN's -2.6% over 5 days may already include it.
findings.independence: None for the same quarter in Europe. Randstad said in July that Germany and the UK had returned to growth, which this partly contradicts.

findings.finding: France, MAN's largest single market (about a quarter of revenue), showed no improvement in labour signals in Q3. The HCOB France composite PMI recovered to 51.1 in September from 48.5 in August, but employment fell for a fifth straight month. Prism'emploi temp FTEs were +0.5% y/y in May, the first positive since 2022. MAN guided France 'flat to slight growth'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: France was flat in Q2 2026 CC and the stock rose 32% on the group print, so France has not set the reaction recently.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside MAN's own flat-to-slight-growth guide, so it lands inside what was guided. It is filed small as a macro proxy. No Prism'emploi national figure for July or August 2026 was found.
findings.independence: Prism'emploi May 2026 barometer (https://www.prismemploi.eu/sites/default/files/2026-07/Barometre_Prismemploi_mai_2026_PACA.pdf, published 2026-07-17) shows France temp stabilising, which offsets. Adecco's 'EMEA ex-France +8%' implies France lagged.

findings.finding: The revenue consensus ($4.91bn, Earnings Whispers) sits at the very top of the implied reported guide ($4.72-4.91bn = +2-6% on Q3 2025's $4.63bn). EPS consensus ($1.01) sits at the guide midpoint and the whisper is $1.03. The revenue line has to print near +6% reported just to meet the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue beat by about 3% and the stock rose 32%. Q3 2025 beat by 0.6% and the stock fell 6.5% on the Q4 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregators quote the EPS bar against the guide. The revenue bar sitting at the top of the reported range is a computed comparison that previews do not print. If the market saw it, the revenue headline would be framed as a likely in-line or miss rather than a beat.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 revenue of $4.63bn per Zacks/8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/871763/000119312525240850/man-ex99_1.htm. The +2-6% reported guide is per Zacks/thestockobserver.

findings.finding: EUR/USD averaged about 1.14 in July, 1.15-1.16 in August and about 1.157 in early-to-mid September 2026. That is slightly stronger than the mid-July level the guide's -2c FX headwind was struck at, though still below Q3 2025's ~1.17. Net, it is a small translation tailwind against the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX is routinely disclosed and looked through. No reaction history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a cents-level item inside the guide's range. It is mechanical and partly modelled already.
findings.independence: ValutaFX USD/EUR 0.8614 on 2026-09-10 (https://www.valutafx.com/history/usd-eur-2026-09-10). Both are aggregators, so the precision is low.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: 9.5% of shares short, 5.38 days to cover (2026-09-30), on a name that squeezed +32% on its last beat. The stock has given back 11% in 20 days and 18% from its high into the print. This leaves asymmetric upside if the reported quarter and the Q4 guide land at or above the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-16: 13.45% short into the print, +32.4%. 2026-01-29: +15.0%. 2025-04-17 (guide cut): -19.1%. Moves are very large in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest has come down (13.45% to 9.5%), so the squeeze fuel is smaller than in July. Days to cover rose back to 5.4 as volume fell. The 20-day drawdown shows the market leaning cautious, not positioned for a beat.
findings.independence: Sweep row records the same settlement. The 20-day run-up of -11.11% is from the sealed baseline.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR 8-Ks since July: only the Q2 2.02 (2026-07-16) and an 8-K 5.02 on 2026-08-11 appointing Paychex CEO John Gibson to the board. Nothing on the print.

rejected_candidates.detail: It is a stale July figure. Current Earnings Whispers consensus is $1.01, matching the company guide midpoint, and that is the bar used.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew. The -11% 20-day run-up and the falling short interest leave the market leaning cautious into the print. My evidence is balanced, slightly positive from peers, so it neither confirms nor fights the drawdown strongly.
lessons_applied: Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): US BLS temp cut from -0.6 to -0.4, because the US is about 15% of revenue against Southern Europe and LatAm growth.
Rule 5 (narrow proxy below the broader series): ASA/Bullhorn cut from +0.4 to +0.2, below the broader BLS series it contradicts.
Rules 9 and 6 (segment, inside guide): Hays cut from -0.3 to -0.2 (Northern Europe about 17%) and France from -0.3 to -0.2 (inside the flat-to-slight-growth guide).
Rule 7 (positioning): the revenue-bar negative cut from -0.4 to -0.3 given 9.5% short and 5.4 days to cover.
'What has worked' (a peer print after the company spoke): peers kept at +0.6.
